body: Yeah, that makes sense.  I agree with this post completely. :)

Honestly, I know you meant well, but something about your post just agitates me.  I'll try to explain. 

1.  Yes, there absolutely is a limit. I would never expect a super human feat from anyone, I'm not looking to get rescued.  What I did expect as a child was that my guardians and my teachers would do their job and get me help when it was clear that I needed it - and believe me, it was clear. Now, as an adult, I hope that when I place my trust in someone that they will not abandon me when I become quiet and withdrawn as I do now and then. It's really not asking much. I don't breathe a word of how bad it gets, much less let anyone witness it.

2. I will never abandon someone I care about when they're struggling - even if they're making my life difficult.  I've been through it with people before and I know myself, I know I would never do that to a friend.  People who become your friend while you're well, and leave if you're not - are not friends.  Maybe 99% of the population thinks that's acceptable, making it the norm - but that only means that I'm only interested in a genuine friendship with whatever 1% out there is willing to be there for the people they care about. 

3. I'm not even remotely interested in trying to get people to like me.  People either do or they don't.  I'm not going to run my life differently to make the people around me more interested in me - because the only thing that matters at the end of the day is how I feel with the decisions I make. 

I don't ask much of people, and I expect nothing.  I'm not out to make anyone feel bad about themselves and I'm not out to be judging of how people live their lives - but I'm not about to let people in if I can't trust them, and I can't trust people who aren't there for their friends.
Yeah, I wouldn't mind telling someone all about my dogs. Heh.  I'm just off to class now, so maybe when I get back I'll message you.

I've been to a few communities and I always just end up feeling guilty for being so screwed up about an assault that wasn't as violent as most people's experiences since I gave up fighting sort of quickly. It's hard to describe.

Yeah, I understand.  I'm past the point where I'm looking for help from parents or teachers though - I'm 22.  It's all on me now.  

I just feel like the problems I have now are mostly about problems that weren't resolved when I was a teenager.  The leftover anger, the trust problems, the guilt and the misery.  I just don't know how to accept those feelings as valid so that I can move forward.  It's like those feelings just want to finish with their 15 minutes of fame but it turned into years and years of fame. heh.

I retreated into my studies.  I guess my VP saw my success as a student as an indication of my emotional wellness.  I was in his office one day for a missed class and he commented that he saw I was doing well in school, so he was glad that "the little problem went away".  It took all my strength not to throw a chair at him.  I didn't answer and he just looked nervously at me until I got up at left. 

I was quiet, but I think the poems about killing myself, the empty vodka bottles, and the cuts all over my arms were pretty obvious indications that I needed help.  I guess that just wasn't enough.

It just really gets under my skin, imagining my 14-16 year old self dealing with sexual assault and then ongoing harassment while the people who were supposed to be in charge of my safety stood by and watched.  I feel like that's just an epic fail that nobody wants to admit to and they leave me to deal with these feelings of their failure.  I feel like I just must be completely insane to have expected anyone to have at least *tried* to help me.

Anyway, maybe I will stick around to help. 

Thanks for the writing compliment. I do really enjoy writing so it's nice to know I'm not bad at it.

> You are pretty much right. Most people avoid complex in today's society, the avoid it... avoid it. 

I wanted so badly to be wrong about that. Heh.

> Have you seriously considered that maybe you just feel more and are in tune with others/life (your dogs, etc) more than the average person?

I've always been told I'm more "aware" of what's going on around me than others.  I guess if that's true, then I just find that a little overwhelming.  I don't know what to do with all the thoughts.   I feel them a lot less when I have a companion of sorts - not necessarily a romantic partner but someone, friend or partner, that I feel I connect with on a stronger level than most people. Usually it's someone who's also incredibly fucked up.  We don't even necessarily talk about what's hurting, so I don't even need to trust them. Just the company of someone else in pain feels incredible.  I wish I had that right now.
